verified.title: build_command resolves the vllm binary outside the venv, so every non-attach serve dies with FileNotFoundError
verified.detail: Line 41 is `vllm_bin = str(Path(sys.executable).resolve().parent / "vllm")`. Ticket 07 step 3 asks for `<sys.executable's directory>/vllm`, but `.resolve()` follows the venv's `bin/python` symlink out to the uv-managed base interpreter, so the directory it takes the parent of is not the venv's `bin/`. `external/vllm-env/bin/python` is a symlink to `~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/python3.12`, so argv[0] becomes `/home/y-guo/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.13-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/vllm`, which does not exist, while `external/vllm-env/bin/vllm` does. Every start-branch launch (M-M1, M-M2, M-M3's non-attach half, and every sample/inject run) raises FileNotFoundError at the `subprocess.Popen(argv, env=env)` of line 201, after jobs/launch.py has already reserved the card and appended the start row. The CPU acceptance cannot see it: A14 prints `' '.join(argv[1:])`, which drops argv[0]. The same defect hits any second venv, since all three `external/*/bin/python` are symlinks. Dropping `.resolve()` gives the venv's own `bin/vllm`; legacy used the absolute path `legacy/serve_preset.py:29`.

Calling the real build_command with the ticket's A14 row gives `argv0 = /home/y-guo/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.13-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/vllm`, `exists = False`, while `external/vllm-env/bin/vllm` exists (-rwxrwxr-x, 343 bytes) and the no-resolve path `Path(sys.executable).parent/'vllm'` resolves to it (True). `subprocess.Popen(['/home/y-guo/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.13-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/vllm','--help'])` -> `FileNotFoundError [Errno 2] No such file or directory`; argv[0] contains slashes so no PATH lookup saves it, and serve()'s non-attach branch calls `subprocess.Popen(argv, env=env)` directly. verified.title: The terminate guard around the check table never fires: a failed model or render check leaves the vLLM server running on the card
verified.detail: Lines 202-208 wrap `_wait_healthy`, `_check_model` and `_check_render` in `try: ... except Exception: proc.terminate(); raise`. All three failures raise `SystemExit` (lines 128, 143, 158), which is a BaseException and not an Exception, so `proc.terminate()` is never reached on any check failure — the guard is dead code. The service piece exits while the vLLM child keeps running: it holds the card, answers on the port, and has no endpoint file and no registry row naming it, so 7.4's attach search cannot find it, `jobs/launch.py`'s 'a port already answering moves the assignment to the next free one' rule pushes the next run onto another port, and the card stays occupied until someone kills the process by hand. M-M2 triggers this deliberately (restart with VLLM_SYSTEM_START_DATE unset so the render check fails), and it is the path a genuine render-vs-server divergence takes on every ordinary launch.
verified.evidence:
Stub run of `svc.main(["serve", ...])` with subprocess.Popen replaced by a recorder (/tmp/svcrev.l9kZkk/t_terminate.py):
-- start branch, GET /v1/models names the wrong model
   SystemExit: models.agent_models.service: GET /v1/models does not name 'gpt-oss-120b' (has ['gpt-oss-20b'])
   subprocess events: ['popen']            <- no terminate
-- start branch, render_ids differs from the chat endpoint
   SystemExit: models.agent_models.service: render_ids diverges from the chat endpoint (3 local ids, 3 server ids)
   subprocess events: ['popen']            <- no terminate
-- start branch, every check passes
   subprocess events: ['popen', 'wait']
models/agent_models/service.py:206:    except Exception:
models/agent_models/service.py:207:        proc.terminate()

verdict.reason:
The Python fact reproduces, but the finding's two load-bearing claims are wrong, and no cited rule requires what it demands.

1) "The guard is dead code" is false. My stub run of svc.serve with subprocess.Popen replaced by a recorder (scratch dir under /tmp, now removed) gives:
   model check SystemExit -> events: ['popen']
   render check SystemExit -> events: ['popen']
   model check HTTPError (urllib.error.HTTPError 500 out of _request) -> events: ['popen', 'terminate']
   all pass -> events: ['popen', 'wait']
So `except Exception: proc.terminate()` at models/agent_models/service.py:206-208 does fire — on every non-SystemExit failure of the three calls (an HTTPError/URLError escaping _request, an exception out of m.module.render_ids). It is skipped only on the three deliberate SystemExit messages.

2) No rule says the service must terminate its child on a failed check. Contracts Part 7.1 (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:3900-3920) specifies the check table and nothing about cleanup; ticket 07 step 5 copies that table and step 7 says only "Then exec/wait on the vLLM process, so the tmux piece lives as long as the server" (.scratch/from-zero/issues/07-model-services.md:104-122). proc.terminate() is the implementer's own extra, not a contracted behaviour.

3) The claimed consequence contradicts the contract that does own this path. Contracts 2.3, "Ending the service pieces" (contracts.md:2021-2045): "`teardown_services` has two callers ... **`jobs/launch.launch` calls it before it returns any outcome other than `up`** (8.1), so a launch whose alive check or `service_check` failed does not leave the service pieces that did come up holding their cards. For each piece entry with `kind: service`, `ssh <host> tmux kill-session -t <session>`". 8.1 repeats it (contracts.md:4413-4417): "**Before it returns any outcome but `up`, `jobs/launch.launch` calls `teardown_services(run_dir)`** ... so a failed launch leaves no service piece holding cards for a run that a `launch_failed` finish row has already closed". A service piece whose check table failed dies, the alive check fails, launch returns `alive_check` and tears the service sessions down — so "the card stays occupied until someone kills the process by hand" is not the designed behaviour, and the 7.4 attach search never needed to find that server. That cleanup lives in jobs/launch.py (ticket 12, a later wave), a file the brief says must not be treated as missing.

4) M-M2 is in ticket 07's "GPU / main session — not yours" list and the reconciliation comment records M-M1..M-M6 as "Not run", so it is not evidence of an observed leak.

Residual, minor and not a spec violation: the guard covers the failure shapes that do not happen and misses the three that do, so a reader can misread it as cleanup on check failure. Whether the service should also terminate its child before exiting is an owner call, not a wave-3 contract breach.

verified.title: check issues no /render, /score or /gen request, so the launch gate passes a probe service whose model routes are broken
verified.detail: `check` (lines 172-218) calls `/health` once and `/encode` three times plus `/decode` once, and never touches `/render`, `/score` or `/gen`. Contracts 7.2 says check 'issues one request of each route against the already-running service', and jobs/launch.py turns its exit code into the `service_check` outcome of 8.1 — the one gate between the service starting and the first loop piece. 7.2 names the exact failure that gets through: `/render` runs `render_ids` in the probe venv, so 'a family's rendering library must be installed in both [venvs] ... and the failure is an ImportError at the start of every sample and inject run'. With `/render` unexercised, that ImportError (and any other render or probe fault that the startup echo cannot show) is discovered by the first loop piece instead, after the cards are taken and the run is recorded as launched. The echo-only check also cannot see a probe that loads but raises on `/score`, which is M-M5's stated content ('/score returns a conf in [0,1] and a label from the checkpoint's labels, /gen returns one line of call text'). `has_inject`, already computed at line 179, is the condition that keeps `/score` and `/gen` out of the render-only case.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with a stub server driving the real svc.check (sample-run cfg, inject=None): exit 0, routes hit ['/health', '/encode', '/encode', '/encode', '/decode'] — no /render, /score or /gen. Matches models/probe_models/service.py:176-217 (client.health(), three client.encode, one client.decode, nothing after). The rule says what the finding claims: contracts 2026-09-17-contracts.md:4007 "check --base-url <url> --run-dir <dir> issues one request of each route against the already-running service, verifies the /health echo and both directions of encode on the <|end|> fixture", and :4013 "jobs/launch.py turns the non-zero exit into the service_check outcome of 8.1". The ticket does not rule the other way — .scratch/from-zero/issues/07-model-services.md:227 repeats "compares, one request per route:" and M-M5 at :455 reads as one check run ("check exits 0 and prints each compared field, /score returns a conf in [0,1] and a label from the checkpoint's labels, /gen returns one line of call text"). No errata entry covers check's route coverage (read contract-errata.md whole; the five wave-3 precheck entries are the agent health timeout, --attach-only's comparison, --attached-to, and eval's heartbeat total). Not on the already-known list, and T07's wave-result.json openFindings/minors/concerns never raise it. The named failure is reachable: models/agent_models/gptoss.py:27 imports openai_harmony inside _to_harmony_messages, so serve()'s models.agent(alias) and selfcheck's family-module import both miss a missing rendering library, and contracts :4071-4079 says "the failure is an ImportError at the start of every sample and inject run"; /health's "render": "ids" is a hardcoded literal at service.py:92, so the echo comparison proves nothing about the route.

minors.title: --attach-only compares the first model card only, while the start branch searches the whole list
minors.detail: `_attach` takes `card = cards[0]` (line 114) and compares that one card's `id`, while `_check_model` in the same file accepts the row's name anywhere in the list (`if row["served_model_name"] not in names`, line 142). A server that lists more than one model card — several `--served-model-name` values, or a LoRA adapter registered beside the base model — makes the attach refuse with a served_model_name mismatch even though it serves the right model, and the refusal message names the other card. minors.title: The probe server's lock covers /score and /gen only; /render, /encode and /decode call the shared tokenizer concurrently
minors.detail: `with lock:` appears at lines 129 and 137 (score, gen) and nowhere else, so `/render` (line 141), `/encode` (line 145) and `/decode` (line 149) run on as many ThreadingHTTPServer threads as there are loop pieces, against one shared tokenizer object. The wave-3 errata line for 7.2 reads 'ThreadingHTTPServer with one lock around every model call'. Measured: harmony's `render_ids` is safe under eight threads, but transformers 5.14.1 mutates shared tokenizer state per call — `tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:955-956` does `if self._tokenizer.encode_special_tokens != split_special_tokens: self._tokenizer.encode_special_tokens = split_special_tokens` — so two overlapping `/encode` calls carrying different `special` values can encode under the other request's flag, silently returning control-token ids for a plain-text body or the reverse. Within one run `special` is constant (`FORMATS[fmt].needs_special`, 7.3) and `check` sends both values before the loop pieces start, so today the window is check-overlapping-a-loop rather than the steady state.

minors.title: serve accepts a checkpoint mode with flags missing and fails later with an error that names nothing
minors.detail: `serve` branches on `--render-only` alone (line 67) and never checks that the other four flags arrived together. Without `--render-only` and without `--score-ckpt`, `Path(args.gen_ckpt)` raises a bare `TypeError: argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object ... not 'NoneType'`, which names neither the flag nor the file — spec.md section 5 requires every refusal to name the field or value. Without `--temperature`, the service starts, takes the card, loads both checkpoints and then answers every `/score` with a 500 carrying `unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'float' and 'NoneType'` from `_softmax_max` (line 22), i.e. the failure lands after the card is taken rather than at startup, which is the shape the param_only refusal at lines 76-79 was written in ('refusing before any card is taken'). The `check` gate does catch the temperature case for an inject run, through the `temperature` echo comparison.

verified.title: probe_eval.run reads stage_extra.labels unconditionally: no None for a generator, and a bare KeyError when a train run writes no stage_extra
verified.detail: Ticket 08 step 5 pins `labels = json.load(train_dir/"meta.json")["stage_extra"]["labels"]` with the explicit rider "`None` for a generator", and contracts 1.4 (`labels` "null for a generator, which has no head") and 2.6 (the `report` hook's `labels` argument is "None for a generator, which has no head") say the same. eval/utils/probe_eval.py:224-225 reads the key unconditionally and hands the result to `method.report` and into the identity block, with no branch on `kind`. Two consequences I ran: (a) a train run whose `meta.json` carries no `stage_extra` at all makes `run` die with a bare `KeyError('stage_extra')` — no message naming the file, against spec.md section 5's "errors name the thing", and 1.5 words done.json's `stage_extra` as present only "for a stage that has one", so a trainer that omits it for a generator (it has no head and no label list) kills every generator eval; (b) when a train run's `stage_extra.labels` holds a list, a generator's `report` receives that list and `probe_report.json`'s `labels` field is written non-null, which 1.4 forbids. The per-ticket reviewer recorded this as cannotVerify (wave-result.json, ticket 08 cannotVerify entry 1); it is now verified by running it. A later ticket that hits it: 10 (eval/methods/cgen.py, cparam.py) once 11/12's trainer decides what to put in stage_extra.

verdict.reason: The finding's own cited rules say the opposite. (1) Ticket 08 pins the exact unconditional expression: issues/08-eval-library-and-classifier-metric.md:67-68 reads `5. \"labels = json.load(train_dir/\"meta.json\")[\"stage_extra\"][\"labels\"]\" (1.3, 8.3). `None` for a generator.` — eval/utils/probe_eval.py:224-225 transcribes it literally; the rider states the value that arrives, not a branch on kind, and spec.md section 1 gives the ticket priority over the contracts anyway. (2) contracts.md:1296 and :2362 define the field as a copy ("copied from the train run's meta.json stage_extra by probe_eval.run, from the same value it hands the method's report hook"), with "null for a generator" as the resulting value, not an override probe_eval must apply. (3) Both failing inputs are states the pinned trainer cannot produce: issues/13-training-loop-and-probe-methods.md:156 pins `registry.write_done(..., stage_extra={"labels": labels})` unconditionally for every train run, and labels comes from `head_labels`, fixed as None for a generator (contracts.md:2338; issues/13:283 "The same seven hook names as ctool, with head_labels returning None"); ticket 10's generator fixture writes `"stage_extra": {"labels": None}` (issues/10-...md:411). The reviewer hand-wrote a meta.json with no stage_extra and one with a stale list for a generator. (4) It is already recorded and deferred by design: wave-result.json ticket 08 cannotVerify entry 1, and the ticket's Comments (issues/08:423-425) "probe_eval.run reads train_meta[\"stage_extra\"][\"labels\"] with no default (eval/utils/probe_eval.py:225), so ticket 13's trainer must always write the key, null for a generator". (5) spec.md section 5's "Errors name the thing" governs the code's own refusals, not Python exceptions on a contract-violating upstream file; probe_eval.py:243,246,247 index guaranteed meta fields the same way, all pinned by ticket 08 step 6.

minors.title: n_events key order is not deterministic: a bare polars group_by makes probe_report.json and report.md differ byte-for-byte between identical runs
minors.detail: eval/methods/ctool.py:145-146 builds `n_events` with `pred_df.group_by("split")` and no `maintain_order=True`, then zips the two result columns into a dict. Polars 1.44.2's grouping order is not stable, so re-running the same eval over the same prediction frame writes `n_events` (and therefore `report.md`'s "## events per split" block) in a different order each time. No number changes; what changes is that two runs of one key produce two different `probe_report.json` byte strings, so the sha1 a downstream generator's `consumed.json` records for the referenced report is not reproducible from the same inputs, and a diff of two eval directories is noisy for no reason. Every other group_by in the file (`_first_crossing`, lines 24 and 32) already passes `maintain_order=True`.

minors.title: An empty test split produces a full frozen block of zeros with a [0.0, 0.0] CI and writes them into done.json metrics, with no refusal
minors.detail: eval/methods/ctool.py:89-91 refuses when the val slice is empty ("no rows with split == 'val' to fit the temperature on"). The test slice has no such check: with `train.predict.splits: [val]` — a legal setting, 5.2 — `test_work` is empty, `_first_crossing` returns an empty frame, `_agg` returns `n: 0` with `coverage/trig_acc/earliness/wrong_spec` all `0.0` (the `if n else 0.0` fallbacks at lines 55-59), and `bootstrap_ci` takes the `df.clear()` branch at probe_eval.py:133 and reports `[0.0, 0.0]` for all three statistics. `probe_eval.run` then writes `coverage@0.1 = 0.0`, `trig_acc@0.1 = 0.0` etc. into done.json's metrics, which 8.2's finish row copies verbatim and eval/method_table.py (ticket 11) prints as if they were measurements. Contracts 1.4 says `frozen` is "the test numbers at that theta", so zeros over zero events are a number with no error — the failure mode 2.5's gates are written against — while the val side already has the corresponding refusal.

minors.title: The first-crossing threshold test runs in float32, so a confidence up to one float32 ulp below theta fires
minors.detail: eval/methods/ctool.py:95 casts the softmax confidence to float32 (`conf = probs.max(axis=1).astype(np.float32)`) before it goes into the `work` frame, and line 31 tests `pl.col("conf") >= theta` against the Python float from `cfg.eval.theta_grid`. Polars downcasts the Float64 literal to the column's Float32 dtype, so the comparison happens in float32: theta 0.9 becomes 0.89999997615814208984375 and a true confidence in [0.89999997615814208984375, 0.9) fires although `eval_tool.py:236`'s float64 `conf >= theta` would not. The window is one float32 ulp, 5.96e-08 near 0.9, so it will essentially never move a real number; it is a deviation from the ported rule all the same, and the f32 dtype is only required for the stored `score` column of fires.parquet (1.4), not for the test. Keeping `conf` float64 in `work` and casting only in the `fires` select would remove it.

verified.title: The offline history holds the stripped action; the pinned live rule appends the raw action, so every live probe text differs from the training text
verified.detail: Line 146 normalises the step's action with `.strip()` and lines 155, 160 and 219 push that stripped string into `history`, which line 182 hands to `probe_input.assemble`. The live side is pinned to append the unstripped value: contracts 7.3 says `agent/loop.py` "appends `(observation.action, observation.observation)` to a list after each `Environment.step`", and errata line 65 refines only the None half ("the loop appends only when `observation.action` is not None, and `data/build_training_dataset.py` does the same") — nothing anywhere says the loop strips. For AppWorld `StepObservation.action` is the raw code-block body: `/home/y-guo/reproduce/new1/data/environments/appworld.py:331-336` does `m = re.search(CODE_BLOCK, reply_text, re.S)` / `code = m.group(1)` / `return StepObservation(code, out, ...)` with `CODE_BLOCK = r"```python\s*(.*?)```"`, so the action of an ordinary reply ends in `\n` (the leading whitespace is eaten by `\s*`, the trailing newline before the closing fence is not). Result: the trained probe read `<code> -> <result>` on every history line and the live probe will read `<code>\n -> <result>`. That is precisely the divergence contracts 1.7 exists to prevent ("the same text nowhere compared, every live number wrong, and no gate anywhere"), it shows up in no number, and no gate compares the two. Both legacy sides stripped (`legacy/pipeline/annotate/build.py:117` and `legacy/pipeline/inject/live_appworld.py:816` `hist.append((code.strip(), out[:TRUNC]))`), so the builder matches legacy and it is the new live rule that moved; the fix is either `agent/loop.py` (ticket 11) stripping too or an errata ruling that pins one spelling for both sides. Ticket 11 written to 7.3 as it stands will hit this.

(1) The targeted line is verbatim ticket text and the ticket wins over contracts (spec.md s1): .scratch/from-zero/issues/09-dataset-builder.md:66-67 "thinking = (gen.reasoning or \"\").strip(), action = (env.action or \"\").strip()" — data/build_training_dataset.py:146 implements exactly that, and the finding concedes the builder matches legacy (legacy/pipeline/annotate/build.py:117). (2) The live half is agent/loop.py, ticket 11, a later wave; the file does not exist and the review scope states its absence is not a finding, so nothing merged can diverge from it yet. minors.title: An empty but non-null action is counted as no_action and left out of history, while the live loop appends it, shifting the whole history window
minors.detail: Lines 146-150 strip first and then test `action == ""`, so a step whose `env.action` is the empty string (an empty or whitespace-only ```python fence: `CODE_BLOCK`'s `\s*` eats the whitespace and `m.group(1)` is `""`, so `StepObservation.action` is `""`, not None) is counted in `events_skipped_no_action` and appends nothing to `history`. The live side appends whenever the action is not None (contracts 7.3, errata line 65), and `data/trajectory_record.py:275` also treats such a step as executed (`content = env_row["result"] if env_row["action"] is not None else no_code`). With `hist_rounds: 3` a dropped entry does not just change one line, it slides the whole window: offline keeps steps 0/2/3 while the live history of the same trajectory is 1/2/3. Contracts 2.5 puts the null-action skip on `env.action` being null and sends every non-null action `split_args` cannot parse to the skip-and-count path the errata renamed `events_skipped_no_call`, so by the contract an empty string belongs in the second counter; ticket 09 step 12 spells the strip-then-test, and the ticket wins, so this is a divergence to rule on rather than a clause broken. Same root as BUILDER-1.

minors.title: A build_call ValueError escapes the event loop without naming the record, the step or the example
minors.detail: Line 164 `call = env.build_call(tool, call_args)` is not guarded. `appworld.build_call` raises `ValueError` for an argument value that holds both a single and a double quote (`data/environments/appworld.py:205-208`) and for a value that needs quoting and ends in an odd number of backslashes (:213-216, the case the owner left open). Both raises name the tool, the key and the value but not the record id, the step or the example id, so the whole build dies over one argument value with nothing pointing at the trajectory to look at — while every other stop in this file names its row (the round trip at :170-174, the empty text at :189, the depth at :191, the prefix at :193, the orphan gen row at :141), which is what contracts 2.5 asks for ("A gate failure stops the build and names the rows"). The both-quotes trigger is reachable from ordinary AppWorld data: a password or message value containing both quote kinds. The raise itself is correct (owner ruling in ticket 09's Comments: "let it raise, do not route around it"); what is missing is the row it happened on.
